Class Status

java.lang.Object
edu.uky.cs.nil.sg.Status
public class Status extends Object
An object that can be periodically updated to reflect the progress of a long-running operation. The current status can be read using the toString() method.

A status has three parts: a message, a count, and a total. The count and total are optional. When a new message is set, the count and total are automatically set to 0.

Updating the message, count, and total are inexpensive operations and can be called many times without significantly impacting performance.

Author:
Stephen G. Ware

  • Method Details

    • toString

      public String toString()

      If the getCount() is 0, this method simply returns the message. If the count is greater than 0, this method returns the message followed by a colon, followed by the current count. If the total is greater than 0, the count is followed by a forward slash and the total and then by the ratio of the count to that total as a percentage in parentheses.

      For example, if the message is "Checking elements" and the count is 0, this method returns "Checking elements".

      If the count is 5 and the total is 0, this method returns "Checking elements: 5".

      If the count is 5 and the total is 10, this method returns "Checking elements: 5/10 (50%)".

      Overrides:
